profile.name: Alistair Macvicar
profile.title: Software developer & researcher
profile.intro: My work spans software development, applied AI research, and connected systems. Before computer science, I worked in telecommunications.

entries.title: Photovoltaic forecasting
entries.summary: Comparing machine learning models for solar generation across multiple buildings and forecast horizons.
body: A study of solar generation forecasts using data from three Flinders University buildings. The work compares temporal and graph-based models, including how models transfer to a newly added system.
This is a preprint. The August 2026 version updates an earlier July release.
entries.citation: Macvicar, A. C., Mahmud, M. A., Stephenson, M., Brinkworth, R., & Senaratne, A. (2026). Machine Learning Approaches for Multi-Horizon and Distributed System Photovoltaic Forecasting. SSRN preprint. https://doi.org/10.2139/ssrn.7369951
entries.label: Preprint

entries.title: Welcome to the Cave
entries.summary: Technology for an interactive performance with actors, audiences, and AI characters.
body: I developed technology for this theatre and research project, coordinating language-model interactions in a 3D environment.
Presented at Adelaide Fringe, the show brought two audience participants together with performers and three AI characters to solve puzzles. Flinders lists my contribution as developer.

entries.title: Tech Lead
entries.summary: Prototypes, connected systems, and technical support for industry collaborations.
body: Designed and built a smart-shopping prototype for Coles Australia, representing Innovation Central Adelaide at Cisco Live MasterTech.

Worked with Cisco specialists on vehicle telemetry and predictive-maintenance capabilities for South Australian ambulance services. Supported student industry projects with project management and technical guidance.

entries.title: LLMs and academic integrity
entries.summary: A talk on using language models for productivity while maintaining academic integrity.
body: Presented “Using LLMs for productivity while maintaining Academic Integrity” at Flinders University, Tonsley.

entries.title: Testing LLMs through games
entries.summary: A talk exploring the limits of language models through game creation.
body: Presented “Testing the limits of current LLMs: Using AI to create games” at Palo Alto Networks in Palo Alto.

entries.title: Vehicle telemetry dashboard
entries.summary: A dashboard prototype for exploring vehicle health, journeys, and live telemetry.
body: Built with Nuxt, Vue, and TypeScript, with charts for engine temperature, fuel use, speed, and distance.
The repository includes a simulated fleet and route data for demonstrating updates and diagnostics.

entries.title: Forget-Me-Note
entries.summary: A browser-based notes editor with local storage and cloud-sync integration.
body: An experiment in organising notes with browser storage, a local-first database, and cloud synchronisation. The code also explores embeddings for working with note content.

entries.title: Pixel Art Converter
entries.summary: A Python tool for converting images and GIFs into pixel art.
body: Groups pixels into blocks and chooses representative colours, with adjustable scale and optional blur. Animated GIFs are processed frame by frame while retaining their timing.

entries.title: Résumé Game
entries.summary: A playable résumé made with Python and Pygame.
body: An experiment in presenting my experience through a small game, with distinct rooms, collision handling, and game state.

entries.title: Mining informativeness in scene graphs
entries.summary: Helping computer vision models focus on relationships that carry useful information.
entries.label: Published paper
body: An image can be described as objects and the relationships between them. But more relationships do not always mean a better description.

This research studies which relationships are useful for downstream tasks. My contribution involved evaluating scene graph data and testing pruning methods, comparing model accuracy and training performance.
entries.citation: Neau, M., Santos, P. E., Bosser, A.-G., Macvicar, A., & Buche, C. (2025). Mining informativeness in scene graphs: Prioritizing informative relations in Scene Graph Generation for enhanced performance in applications. Pattern Recognition Letters, 189, 64–70. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.patrec.2025.01.008

entries.title: Control Systems Engineer
entries.summary: Web portals and remote telemetry for industrial IoT systems.
body: Developed a web portal for monitoring the health and effectiveness of industrial IoT solutions, with role-based access and a modular approach to customer deployments.
Designed, programmed, and tested a remote solar and battery monitoring solution intended for more than 30 locations across Australia, using microcontrollers, satellite connectivity, and LoRaWAN.

entries.title: Bachelor of Computer Science
entries.summary: A foundation in software, databases, and computer science. GPA 6.6.
body: Completed a Bachelor of Computer Science at Flinders University with a GPA of 6.6.
Alongside my studies, I worked in teaching and research, connecting the theory to practical software and computer vision problems.
highlights: College of Science and Engineering Honours Scholarship · 2024

entries.title: Research Assistant
entries.summary: Computer vision, AI performance, and real-world telemetry problems.
body: Conducted computer vision research with Dr Paulo Santos and Maëlic Neau through a College of Science and Engineering Summer Research Award. The work examined scene graph data for visual question answering.

Further work included coordinating multiple language models for a Flinders University and Adelaide Fringe collaboration involving audiences and improvisational actors, and vehicle telemetry work with Cisco and Innovation Central Adelaide.
Research also includes machine learning for solar power forecasting.
highlights: Scene graph research published in Pattern Recognition Letters

entries.title: Academic Tutor
entries.summary: Teaching relational database modelling and Java programming.
body: Delivered tutorials and practical sessions in relational database modelling and Java programming for undergraduate and postgraduate students.
Provided assessment feedback and marking across multiple topics, supporting more than 200 students.
highlights: Tutorials, practical sessions, and assessment feedback

entries.title: Director
entries.summary: Managing a telecommunications business and delivering NBN projects.
body: Designed, developed, and installed telecommunications solutions for the NBN project with multiple delivery partners.
Worked across Australia to support training, rollouts, and upgrades. Managed clients, finances, and a team of three other technicians.

entries.title: Leading Hand
entries.summary: Leading a team of more than 50 technicians on the HFC NBN project.
body: Led a team of more than 50 technicians on the HFC NBN project.
Kept working on the tools to stay close to the technology and understand what the team needed on site.

entries.title: Hybrid Fibre-Coaxial Technician
entries.summary: Technical training for work on the NBN network.
body: Completed Hybrid Fibre-Coaxial Technician training with JB Hunter for the NBN network.

entries.title: Supervisor
entries.summary: My first job became my first experience managing a team.
body: A job I started as a teenager turned into my first management experience, learning how to support a team and keep things moving.

entries.title: Hermes
entries.summary: An open-source social app with one-to-one chats, group messaging, and friends lists.
body: One of my larger personal projects: a functioning social platform with one-to-one and group messaging and friends lists.
I built both the frontend and backend, working through the API and database design needed to connect all the moving parts.
